method: WebSearch for initial discovery (session WebSearch quota was exhausted after ~11 queries, unusually early), after which discovery continued via WebFetch against Google News RSS feeds (news.google.com/rss/search) to surface candidate headlines/dates/sources, followed by direct WebFetch reads of the underlying publisher articles (Tribune India, TrueScoop, Babushahi, Swarajya, Wikipedia, etc.) to confirm company identity, figures, sectors and dates before inclusion. Several publisher URLs could not be reached directly (404s on guessed slugs, Google News redirect pages that render as JS shells rather than article text, DuckDuckGo/Bing CAPTCHA blocks) — where a finding rests on strong multi-outlet snippet corroboration rather than a single deep-read article, this is noted in the entry's follow_through_status or in negative_notes. Only individually-named, non-India-headquartered companies with a dated, sourced signing/announcement were included in the main list; aggregate summit press-release totals and unnamed 'X companies signed Y crore' claims were excluded and logged in negative_notes instead.

negative_notes: Punjab is thinly covered for individually-verifiable foreign MoUs relative to Haryana. Several leads were investigated and could not be confirmed to the bar required for inclusion: (a) 'CM Mann's foreign trip yields brilliant results - 9 major companies choose Punjab' (TrueScoop, 2025-12-20) — headline claims nine companies but no article text with individual names could be retrieved; excluded. (b) Several UAE-based companies were reported as 'expected to scale up investment in Punjab' around the 2019 Progressive Punjab summit (Gulf News) but no specific company names or dated MoUs were found for the 2021-2026 window. (c) The February 2023 (5th) Progressive Punjab Investors' Summit produced almost no individually-named foreign-company coverage in the sources checked; notably, CM Mann himself downplayed formal MoUs at that summit, telling press 'We're signing Memorandum of Dil Se, not MoU' (Indian Express, 2023-02-25), suggesting that edition deliberately avoided big splashy foreign MoU announcements in favour of informal, sector-specific engagement.

HPCL-Mittal Energy Limited (HMEL) announced a Rs 2,600 crore speciality/fine chemicals investment at the Progressive Punjab Investors' Summit 2026, attributed in press to 'LN Mittal'. HMEL is excluded from the main list: it is an India-incorporated joint venture (50% HPCL, a state-owned Indian company; 50% Mittal Energy Investments, part of the Mittal family's investment vehicle) rather than a foreign-headquartered company, and coverage did not support treating it as an ArcelorMittal-branded investment.

Escorts Kubota Limited (Faridabad-area tractor manufacturing) is excluded from the Haryana list on the same basis: it is an India-incorporated company, majority-owned by Kubota Corporation (Japan) since 2022, not a foreign-HQ'd entity in its own right. A separate, less ambiguous Kubota Corporation roadshow commitment (Oct 2025, Rs 2,000+ crore) is included above with MEDIUM confidence because its relationship to the existing Escorts Kubota entity is unclear.

Haryana's 'Happening Haryana - Global Investors Summit' (Gurugram, reported September 2023) is frequently cited as having produced '357 MoUs worth Rs 5.84 lakh crore', but no source found broke this aggregate down into individually named foreign companies; excluded as an unverifiable aggregate claim, though the event itself is logged under summits_covered.

Six MoUs worth a combined Rs 1,185 crore were reported signed during CM Saini's October 6, 2025 Japan visit, with the delegation meeting nine named companies (AISIN, Air Water, TASI, Nambu, Denso, Sojitz, Nissin, Kawakin, Toppan) — but no source clearly stated which six of the nine were actual signatories versus which were meeting/discussion partners only. Excluded from the main list pending clearer attribution, despite all nine being plausible real Japanese companies.

'Nine Japanese companies to invest Rs 5,000 crore in Haryana, Gurugram Global City Project underway' (New Indian Express, 2025-10-17) — could not retrieve the underlying article text to identify the nine companies; excluded as an unverifiable aggregate claim.

IKEA (brand Swedish; corporate structure via Ingka Group, headquartered in the Netherlands) has an existing operational Gurugram store and was reported in July-August 2026 press as in discussion with the Haryana CM about further expansion (~Rs 3,500-4,000 crore, conflicting figures across sources). No clear dated MoU signing event was found — this reads as ongoing relationship-building rather than a discrete new MoU — so it was excluded from the main list as a monitoring lead rather than a verified finding.

Godrej Industries Group (Rs 20,000 crore MoU, Happening Haryana 2.0, Mumbai, August 24 2026), Reliance Industries (Rs 8,646 crore, Jhajjar township, June 2026), and Anant Raj (Rs 20,000-25,000 crore data centres, June 2026) are all India-headquartered companies and were excluded per the task's foreign-only scope, despite being the largest individual MoU figures found in the Haryana search.

Honda signed an MoU with the Haryana government (reported September 29, 2025) to set up a construction-and-demolition (C&D) waste processing plant. This is a genuine, dated, named MoU, but no investment figure could be found and the project is a waste-management facility rather than a manufacturing/industrial investment in the spirit of the task; omitted from the main list as low-significance, noted here for completeness.
HS Hyosung's Rs 1,740 crore investment (reported February 2025) is for a plant in Nagpur, Maharashtra, not Haryana or Punjab — a false-positive surfaced during search and explicitly excluded.

Emaar Properties' (Dubai) shopping mall project is in Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir, not Punjab — a false-positive surfaced during search (name collision with 'Punjab' region searches) and explicitly excluded.

This session's WebSearch tool quota was exhausted unusually early (after roughly 11 queries), well short of the normal per-session allowance, forcing a pivot to WebFetch-against-Google-News-RSS as the primary discovery mechanism for the remainder of the sweep. This is a less precise discovery method than direct WebSearch and likely missed some findable MoUs, particularly for Punjab; a follow-up sweep with a fresh WebSearch quota would likely surface additional verifiable entries, especially for Punjab's 2021-2024 period which is under-covered here.
